The mathematical proof, not numerical testing, covers infinite sequences.

originality.rationale: The 1984 five-page Fritsch-Butland paper was inspected in full: it specifies the signed harmonic selector (p.300 formula 2 and p.301 formula 5, uniform grid) and proves monotonicity, without asserting a perturbation variation norm. The 1987 Edelman-Micchelli inspected pages establish admissible slope geometry, not a norm of differences of interpolants. The inspected 2019 Arandiga-Yanez sections quantify interpolation accuracy/monotonicity and reductions of mean formulas, not the sharp 59/27 two-input BV factor. Relevant indexed findings on different interpolation range, smoothers and nonlinear medians do not imply this coefficient. A historical unindexed theorem remains possible.

value.rationale: The classical harmonic-mean Hermite interpolation method is individually variation-preserving, but the new exact all-grid two-input perturbation gain 59/27 quantifies hidden oscillatory sensitivity. A single-jump near-plateau witness and a local three-cell mechanism explain sharpness. This is a natural complete operator-stability invariant, independent of arbitrary finite truncation or a known numerical table.
